questions.question: What is an emergency fund for?

choices.label: Your car insurance payment that's due next month
A car repair you need to get to work
Concert tickets that are on sale this week

questions.explain: It's for urgent costs you couldn't plan for. A bill you know is coming belongs in your budget, and a sale is a want, not an emergency.

questions.question: Your housing and meal plan are paid through financial aid. What should you count as monthly essentials?

choices.label: Rent and meals anyway, to be safe
Only what you still pay each month, like phone and transportation
Nothing, since you're covered

questions.explain: Count what you still pay yourself. Prepaid costs don't need to come out of your fund.

questions.question: What's a good first goal for an emergency fund?

choices.label: One month of essentials
Six months, since smaller amounts don't really help
Whatever's left at the end of the month

questions.explain: One month is a realistic place to start and covers many common surprises. Every bit helps, and you can build toward three or six months later.

questions.question: Where is a good place to keep your emergency fund?

choices.label: In checking, so it's easy to reach
In a separate high-yield savings account
In an index fund, since it can grow more

questions.explain: A separate savings account keeps it from being spent by accident. Investments can drop in value right when you need cash.

questions.question: What matters most when choosing where to keep it?

choices.label: It's insured by the FDIC (banks) or NCUA (credit unions)
It has the highest rate you can find, even if it isn't insured
It gives you a bonus for opening the account

questions.explain: Insurance protects your money, up to the legal limit, even if the institution runs into trouble. A higher rate or a bonus doesn't matter if the money isn't safe.

questions.question: Your laptop dies a week before finals and you need it to finish your work. Is that a good use of your emergency fund?

choices.label: Yes. It's urgent, you couldn't plan for it, and you need it
No. Wait until after finals and put it on a credit card
No. Electronics should always come out of your regular budget

questions.explain: A laptop that dies right before finals is urgent and you couldn't have planned for it, which is what the fund is for. Putting it on a credit card can cost more if you can't pay it off right away.

questions.question: You used part of your fund for a surprise medical bill. How should you think about that?

choices.label: You used it for what it's for, and you can rebuild it a little at a time
You made a mistake, so it's better to stop saving for a while
You need to put all of it back next month

questions.explain: Using your fund for a real emergency is exactly what it's for, so it isn't a mistake. You rebuild it at your own pace, a little at a time.

questions.question: Which of these should you leave out when you add up your monthly essentials?

choices.label: Streaming, eating out, and shopping
Your phone bill
The cost of getting to class or work

questions.explain: Essentials are the costs you can't skip, like a phone and transportation. Extras such as streaming, eating out, and shopping stay out of the total.

questions.question: Your income changes a lot from month to month. Which goal is worth considering?

choices.label: Six months of essentials
One month, since more than that isn't needed
The size of your biggest paycheck

questions.explain: When your income swings, a bigger cushion helps you get through the slow months. You can still start with one month and build up.

questions.question: A savings app says it helps you save. What should you check before you trust it with your emergency fund?

choices.label: That your money is held at an FDIC-insured bank
That it has lots of five-star reviews
That it invests your money so it grows faster

questions.explain: Not every app is a bank. Check that your money is held at an insured bank, so it's protected up to the legal limit. Investing it would put your safety net at risk right when you need cash.
